Sara: heads-up — after the attn_kernel_v3 rollout we saw a new OOM pattern on a few Dedicated nodes. Not a single large alloc; looks like fragmentation from many small frees while KV prefix cache warms. Repro / quick profile included below.

Mike: which fleet and which model? can you paste the nvidia-smi / torch snapshot?

Sara: ran on ded-gpu-a100-1, model=llama-13B, batch=4, seq=2048. Quick snapshot:```
> GPU 0: 40/80 GiB used (processes: redwood_infer)
> torch.cuda.memory_reserved(): 39.7 GiB
> torch.cuda.memory_allocated(): 37.1 GiB
> free fragments: many small holes ~2-16 MiB each, total free ~7 GiB but cannot satisfy a 10 GiB contiguous alloc -> OOM
```

Devon: this smells like max_split_size_mb interplay with our allocator's expandable_segments. When kernel routing switched to tiled-attn kernels we ended up with slightly larger per-kv allocations but many more churned buffers on batched requests. The allocator kept creating small segments instead of coalescing.

Akiko: interesting — did you try lowering max_split_size_mb? that usually forces larger contiguous segments to split less often. also garbage_collection_threshold could make GC run earlier to defragment. What values are you testing? @Sara

Sara: quick experiments:
- baseline: expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=512, garbage_collection_threshold=0.6 -> reproducible OOM at step ~120
- tweak A: expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=128, garbage_collection_threshold=0.6 -> passed to step 500 w/ slightly higher steady CPU for GC
- tweak B: expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=64, garbage_collection_threshold=0.25 -> no OOM, lower peak reserved memory, though perf p50 token latency +4%

Mike: can you paste the micro-profile (cpu/gpu spans) that points to where fragmentation happens?

Sara: gist of the perf (truncated):```
[profile]
kv_cache_alloc_small: 18% (lots of 2-16MiB mallocs)
attention_kernel_route: 12%
cudaMalloc/cudaFree: 15% (spiky)
kernel_dispatch_wait: 20% (due to memory stalls)
```

Devon: that matches the theory — many small KV allocations on warmup cause cudaFree churn and tiny holes. Two pragmatic routes: (1) make allocator more aggressive on reuse/merging (compact_reclaim pass), (2) tune knobs to reduce split behavior and force earlier GC. Seems tweak B is promising but we need to quantify perf/regressions.

Akiko: I pushed a little test harness to CI: `ci/alloc-frag-suite` that runs the repro across model sizes + batch shapes, comparing baseline vs tweak B. ops-bot kicked it off:

ops-bot: CI run started: https://ci.redwood/example/alloc-frag-suite/3421

Sara: initial CI results (summary):
- llama-7B: baseline OK, tweak B p50 +2% and memory stable
- llama-13B: baseline OOM in 60% runs, tweak B stable but p50 +4-6%
- llama-70B: baseline immediate OOM on ded-gpu-a100-1, tweak B passed with 1.1x CPU GC overhead

Mike: tradeoff looks acceptable for Dedicated where uptime matters. For Hosted we should be cautious about latency hits. Can we implement a dynamic policy: aggressive knobs only when fragmentation metric > threshold? e.g., if free_fragment_count > N then set garbage_collection_threshold=0.25 and disable expandable_segments for that worker.

Devon: yes — we already emit fragment metrics in the runtime. A short-lived per-worker policy is doable and avoids cluster-wide latency regressions. I'll prototype a toggle: `allocator.compact_mode` (auto) that flips those three knobs temporarily during warmup.

Akiko: please also add a trace point around `kv_cache_alloc_small` and measure CPU overhead of more frequent GC. we need a regression dashboard.

Sara: action items:
- Devon: prototype `allocator.compact_mode` and test auto-flip heuristic (frag_count, biggest_free < needed_alloc) — due EOD Thu
- Akiko: add perf traces + CI matrix for latency regression guardrails — due Fri
- Mike: evaluate rollout plan for Dedicated pools (suggest opt-in per-customer) — ping by Mon

Mike: thanks — gentle reminder to tag any config flags behind feature gates. :thumbsup:

Sara: will post a short RFC once Devon has prototype. thx everyone. :rocket:
